newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: New fire put out in Saudi tent camp, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: New fire put out in Saudi tent camp, no casualties.

text.p: A small fire broke out but was quickly extinguished on Thursday in a pilgrim tent city in Saudi Arabia where a blaze earlier this week killed 343 people, the official Saudi Press Agency (SPA) said.
The Saudi civil defence authority said the fire, which was extinguished in minutes, caused no damage at the encampment in Mena, 11 km (seven miles) from the Islamic holy city of Mecca, SPA said.
The agency did not say what caused the fire. Diplomats and witnesses said the blaze on Tuesday was caused by the explosion of a gas cylinder.
The agency quoted the civil defence as saying all of its units were on full alert and deployed throughout the areas where pilgrims were staying in tens of thousands of tents.
Tuesday's blaze injured some 1,290 pilgrims and consumed 70,000 tents, but Saudi authorities said they had rebuilt most of them to house the pilgrims left without shelter.

The official media did not give the nationalities of the dead but diplomats said most were from the Indian subcontinent. The fire also engulfed Iranian, Syrian, Lebanese, Egyptian, Sudanese, Yemeni and Moroccan sections of the encampment.
Embassies said they still had no final figures for their dead, adding that many bodies were charred beyond recognition.
Some two million pilgrims performed this year's haj pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia, which ended on Thursday with Eid al-Adha, the feast of sacrifice.
